conviction_note: Public Baltic averages and Genco's own fixtures point to Q3 TCE about 11% above Q2 ($24,486), so EPS should land at or a little above the $1.24-1.33 consensus and the dividend above $0.90. Q4-to-date peer fixtures (Genco $30,102 for 66% of days, Pangaea $21,423 QTD) point to a firm Q4, and the stock was sold 5-8% into the print with shorts building. Against that, Genco's record print was sold on 'cycle near the crest' worries, and the consensus bar has two disagreeing sources. So p_up is only 56 on an abs move of 4.5, giving +0.54. The findings sum (+1.5) is larger because each finding is sized alone; the gap is the peer's sold-beat reaction weighing on p_up.

next_guide.company_current_guide: No earnings guide. The company gives Q4 2026 off-hire of about 280 days (vs 460 in Q3), five Kamsarmax newbuild deliveries in Q3/Q4 with $122m capex funded by up to $129m debt, and a NTM FFA-based FCF of $4.1/share at about $22,000/day fleetwide (Q2 call, 2026-08-06, https://www.starbulk.com/media/uploads_file/2026/08/11/p1jvp1o3tpm511dv2an41sthtbd4.pdf)
next_guide.basis: Q4 coverage should come in above Q3 actuals. Peer Q4-to-date fixtures are above their Q3 actuals (Genco $30,102 vs $27,539, Pangaea $21,423 vs $20,414), mid-November Baltic Supramax is $23.2k vs a $21.3k Q3 average, Capesize has recovered to $42.8k after an October dip, and Q4 off-hire days drop by 180.

findings.finding: Public Baltic averages imply Star Bulk's Q3 TCE about +11% QoQ, to roughly $27,000/day vs Q2's $24,486. Q2-to-Q3 index averages: Capesize about $37.6k to $44.9k (+19%), Panamax $19.2k to $20.3k (+6%), Supramax $19.4k to $21.3k (+10%), weighted by SBLK's Q2 revenue mix (35% Cape / 28% Kamsarmax-Panamax / 37% Ultra-Supra). The company's own sensitivity ($1,500/day = $72m EBITDA a year, about $0.16/share a quarter) puts adjusted EPS near $1.40-1.45 before extra off-hire. That compares with a $1.33 / $1.24 consensus and implies a Q3 dividend above $0.90 under the full-payout policy.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 beat consensus by about $0.21 with a near-doubled dividend; the reported reaction was +3.4%, unconfirmed (allinvestview), and shares are down 7.3% since. Baseline history is 6-K noise and not usable.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus EPS of $1.33 is only 10% above Q2's $1.21, although a +11% TCE move on an operating-leverage name should lift EPS about 20%. If the Street had fully marked Q3 to the index, consensus would sit near the $1.37 whisper or above, and the stock would not have fallen 7% since the last print. The partial explanation is 460 Q3 off-hire days (separate finding), which analysts may already model.
findings.independence: Proxy: index averages, not company fixtures. Monthly averages from https://www.handybulk.com/baltic-dry-index/2026/july/, https://handybulk.com/baltic-dry-index/2026/august/, https://handybulk.com/baltic-dry-index/2026/april/, /may/ and /june/. The sensitivity and revenue mix come from the Q2 call transcript (https://www.starbulk.com/media/uploads_file/2026/08/11/p1jvp1o3tpm511dv2an41sthtbd4.pdf). The same direction is confirmed independently by Genco's realised Q3 TCE (next finding).

findings.finding: Genco reported Q3 2026 TCE of $27,539/day, +13.5% vs its Q2 $24,273 (Newcastlemax $41,315, Capesize $36,980, Ultramax $20,629, Supramax $18,395), and raised its dividend to $1.05 from $0.80. Its Q2 TCE was within 1% of Star Bulk's $24,486, so the same step-up points to SBLK Q3 TCE around $27,000-27,500. Genco's realised Q3 came in about 4% below its own early-August Q3-to-date estimate of $28,587.
findings.link: Same dry-bulk segments and the same spot-exposed model: Genco is Capesize/Newcastlemax plus Ultra/Supramax, about 72% of SBLK's revenue mix (35% Cape + 37% Ultra/Supra). SBLK also has 28% Kamsarmax/Panamax, where Q3 index gains were smaller (+6%). Q2 2026 fleet TCEs were $24,273 vs $24,486.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Genco's own Q3 print on this line drew -3.88% the next session per finviz/Earnings Whispers, or +2.3% per an aggregator. SBLK's Q2 beat drew roughly flat to +3.4%.
findings.why_not_priced: Genco reported two weeks ago, after Star Bulk last spoke (Aug 6), and SBLK fell about 5% in the last 5 sessions rather than rising, so the read-across is not visibly in the price. The Genco miss vs its own Q3-to-date guide shows realised can lag the to-date marks, which caps the size.
findings.independence: Different source from the index finding (company-realised fixtures, not Baltic averages). Genco Q2 numbers: https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/?p=1143873

findings.finding: The peer's strong print was sold. Genco posted multi-year-high TCE and a record $1.05 dividend on 2026-11-04 and traded -3.88% to $24.71. Earnings Whispers cites smaller upside revisions (full-year dividend outlook up only about $0.05 vs about $0.65 the quarter before), Capesize falling from about $50k in September to a floor near $30k in October, and investors 'pricing a cycle closer to its crest than its trough'.
findings.link: Same sector, same Capesize/Ultramax exposure (about 72% of SBLK revenue mix), same full-payout dividend model judged on the quarter-on-quarter dividend step. Investors read the two names together.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: SBLK's last print (Q2 beat plus dividend raise) drew a modest reaction (+0-3.4%, unconfirmed), then a 7.3% drift down. Beats here are not rewarded strongly.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: SBLK is already -7.9% over 20 days, consistent with the same 'crest' worry. What is not priced is whether the market treats SBLK's beat-and-raise the same way. Capesize has since recovered to $42.8k (Nov 13), which weakens the 'October floor' part of the bear argument.
findings.independence: An aggregator reports GNK +2.3% after the print, conflicting (https://www.allinvestview.com/earnings/GNK/q3-2026/). The October Capesize dip is confirmed independently (Oct BCI average 4,053 vs Sept 5,812, low 3,249 on Oct 16: https://handybulk.com/baltic-dry-index/2026/october/).

findings.finding: Q4-to-date evidence points to a firm or higher Q4 coverage disclosure. Genco has 66% of Q4 days fixed at $30,102 (Newc/Cape $40,187 at 64%, Ultra/Supra $22,145 at 67%), +9% vs its Q3 actual. Pangaea's Q4 QTD is $21,423 on 5,040 days vs $20,414 in Q3 (+5%). Baltic 13 Nov: Capesize $42,798 (+8.6% w/w), Supramax $23,203 (vs $21.3k Q3 average), Panamax $19,063 (vs $20.3k). Star Bulk's own Q4 off-hire falls to about 280 days from 460 in Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No usable SBLK history on the Q4-coverage line. Genco's Q4 coverage (+9% QoQ) did not stop its stock falling, which is why this is not sized larger.
findings.why_not_priced: The October Capesize slide (BCI low 3,249 on Oct 16) dominated sentiment and SBLK fell into the print. If the market were pricing a Q4 coverage above Q3, SBLK would not trade 18% off its high with sentiment 'slightly bearish'. The November Capesize recovery is two weeks old and SBLK has not followed it.
findings.independence: Pangaea (https://finviz.com/news/417887/pangaea-logistics-solutions-ltd-reports-financial-results-for-the-third-quarter-ended-september-30-2026, 2026-11-05) and the Baltic weekly (https://www.shipuniverse.com/?p=27832, 2026-11-13) are separate sources. Off-hire days come from SBLK's Q2 call.

findings.finding: Star Bulk guided about 460 off-hire (drydock) days in Q3 2026 vs about 280 in Q4 and 450 for all of 2027 (Q2 call, 2026-08-06). That is about 3.7% of roughly 12,300 ownership days, worth roughly $12m of TCE revenue (about $0.11/share) in Q3. It drags the reported quarter against a pure index read but improves Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No history found on off-hire surprises for SBLK.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it is company guidance, so analysts likely model it. This is the main reason consensus EPS ($1.33) is below a naive index-implied figure. It is filed because it sits inside what the company guided, and so caps the beat.
findings.independence: Same document as the sensitivity used in the first finding (shared document, not double counted: this finding is the offset).

findings.finding: SBLK was sold into the print: -5.25% over 5 days and -7.91% over 20 days to $26.54, 18% off its 52-week high and about 14% below the ~$31 consensus target. findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: After the Q2 beat the stock drifted -7.3%. Peer GNK, also sold into its print, fell again on a record print, so a low bar has not guaranteed a pop in this sector this season.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself. The point is the setup: a full-payout name trading at a 52-week-low area while Q3/Q4 rate evidence is up QoQ. If the market were already pricing a Q3 dividend of about $1+, the stock would sit nearer its post-Q2 range ($26.45-32.88).

findings.finding: FINRA short interest rose for three settlements in a row: 2.96m (Sep 30, 1.42 DTC), 3.70m (Oct 15, 2.36), 3.98m (Oct 30, 3.60). That is about 3.6% of shares, alongside a -12.1 vol-point 25-delta skew (calls bid) and put/call OI of 0.83.
findings.why_not_priced: Shorts building into a strong-rate print gives modest cover-fuel on a good dividend. It is not crowded (3.6 days), so this is small. The call skew already says the option market leans up, so a positive sign here agrees with the skew and is partly priced.
findings.independence: Skew from the sealed baseline (options v7). Separate source.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-09 Star Bulk agreed to sell a 35% ownership interest in two 2026-built Kamsarmaxes (Star Ellie, Star Bella) to Hermes World Maritime, keeping commercial and technical management. No price was disclosed. It is likely a cash inflow, possibly with a gain or a non-controlling interest, recognised in Q4.
findings.why_not_priced: Terms are undisclosed, so the call may quantify proceeds or a newbuild mark-to-market (management cited about $56m MTM on the newbuild programme on Aug 6). The near-zero reaction suggests nobody priced proceeds. Small, one-off-like.

findings.finding: On 2026-08-10, at Star Bulk's request, it terminated the agreement to buy 16 Genco vessels for $470.5m contingent on Diana's Genco bid. That removes a large cash use and keeps the full-payout dividend and buyback capacity intact (cash about $532m, debt $955m at Aug 6).
findings.why_not_priced: Public for three months and almost certainly priced. Filed because it bears on the Q3 payout and on capital-allocation questions on the call.

findings.finding: On the Q2 call (2026-08-06) management put the HSFO-VLSFO scrubber spread at $150-170/t, about $250 in Singapore, because of the Middle East conflict, and said it 'really boosts' the yield of SBLK's scrubber-fitted vessels. That supports an SBLK TCE premium over the index in Q3 if the spread persisted.
findings.why_not_priced: The spread level through Q3 was not verified here. It is a premium the index read in the first finding does not capture, but analysts heard the same call. Small.
findings.independence: none (same call transcript as the off-hire finding; no Q3 spread series checked)
